title: The Underbog
body: The Underbog lies beneath Serpent Lake in Coilfang Reservoir, a drowned cavern where the fungus of the marsh grows unchecked. Light comes mostly from the glowing caps of the fungus, and the water lies dark and still. Bog giants and shamblers wade through its pools, underbats hang in the gloom, fen rays and lykul wasps drift over the water, and underbog lords and lurkers move among the giant mushrooms. The naga hold part of it: Wrathfin myrmidons, sentries and warriors keep watch, crying out for their master and for Illidan, and Murkblood Broken fight beside them. Its masters are a strange company, and the deepest pools hide worse than the bog giants. The sporelings of Sporeggar have errands here, and the Cenarion Expedition has druids to find.

parts.body: Not every master of the Underbog is named in the sporelings' tales. In its deep water swam a hydra called Ghaz'an, which rose against those who came near and fought them in its own pools. It died there, in the drowned cavern it had ruled.

title: Hungarfen
body: Hungarfen is a fungal giant, a hulking thing of cap and stalk that dwells in the Underbog among the bog giants and shamblers. Beside it grows a great plant known as the Underspore, and the giant keeps close to it. Hungarfen does not fight alone, for the cavern floor seems to answer it: around its foes small mushrooms spring up one after another, swelling until they burst in clouds of choking spores.

parts.body: To the sporelings of Sporeggar, Hungarfen is one of the leaders of the spore giants, with whom they are at war whether they like it or not. T'shu says the giant has tended the Underspore to perfection for millennia, and that it would break its spirit if something happened to the plant. All is fair in mushrooms and war, the sporelings say.
sources: quest 9717 description (at war with the spore giants, whether we like it or not; all is fair in mushrooms and war; Hungerfen has been tending a very special plant, known as the Underspore, to perfection for millennia; it would break his spirit)

parts.body: Sorely wounded, Hungarfen roared in pain and stood its ground in a cloud of foul spores, but the fungal giant fell all the same, there beside the plant it kept so close to.
sources: creature_text 17770 group 0 (Hungarfen roars in pain.) and boss_hungarfen.cpp (at 20 percent health it roots itself, emotes and casts Foul Spores)

parts.body: A frond cut from the Underspore went back to T'shu at Sporeggar, who made a sound much like snorting laughter. The spore giants' morale would surely be at an all time low once they realized what had been done, the sporeling said, unless they were so incensed that they attacked again soon.
sources: quest 9717 reward text (snorting laughter; morale of the spore giants at an all time low; or so incensed that they'll attack us again soon)

title: Swamplord Musel'ek
body: Swamplord Musel'ek is a Broken who hunts for the naga in the Underbog, and he is deadly with a bow. He lays freezing traps, marks his quarry and picks it off with aimed shots, or looses volleys of arrows into a crowd, and he keeps a great bear called Claw as his pet. When the bear works itself into a frenzy, he shouts at it to obey him and kill the intruders at once. To his foes he promises a fight to the death, or that he will end it quickly.

parts.body: Earthbinder Rayge, a druid found alive in the Underbog, knows the truth about the bear. He and Windcaller Claw were jumped by Musel'ek while investigating, and the swamplord can control animals, even druids. Claw was caught in bear form and is now his pet, and Rayge dares not take cat form himself, or he would be next.
sources: npc_text 9121 (gossip 7521: Claw and I were investigating this place when we were jumped by Swamplord Musel'ek. He can control animals, even druids! ... Claw was caught in bear form at the time, and is now the swamplord's pet. I don't dare change into cat form)

parts.body: Beaten down, the bear broke free of the swamplord's hold and became Windcaller Claw again, a tauren druid. How embarrassing, he said, to be taken as a pet by a hunter. He owed his rescuers his life, but he would find his own way out now, and perhaps pick up Rayge along the way.

title: The Black Stalker
body: The Black Stalker waits at the far end of the Underbog, a great beast of the marsh that stalks on long legs. It is no simple animal. It crackles with lightning, chaining bolts from one foe to the next and laying static charges upon them, and it can lift its enemies helplessly into the air and hurl them about, so that they come crashing down again.

parts.body: To the sporelings she is an old terror. Khn'nix of Sporeggar names the marsh walkers the greatest danger to the sporelings through their history, and the Black Stalker the great mother of them all. With the spore giants already pressing on Sporeggar, the village cannot afford another attack from its ancient enemies, so Khn'nix wants her dead, and her brain brought back as proof.
sources: quest 9719 description (Historically the greatest danger to my people has been from the marsh walkers; new problems from spore giants; eliminate the great mother of the marsh walkers, known as The Black Stalker; bring me her brain as proof)

parts.body: For all the lightning that crackled about the great beast and its strange hold over the air, the Black Stalker fell at the far end of the Underbog, and the storm died away.
sources: boss_the_black_stalker.cpp (fixed spawn 138323, map 546 only; Levitate, Chain Lightning, Static Charge)

parts.body: Khn'nix did not revel in such butchery, but the pain the great mother and her brood had brought the sporelings over the centuries was unspeakable. Another of her progeny would transform to replace her, the sporeling knew, yet that would take time, and Sporeggar would have some breathing room from the marsh walkers for a while.
sources: quest 9719 reward text (Normally I would not revel in such butchery; pain over the centuries is unspeakable; another of her progeny will transform to replace her, but that will take time and give us some breathing room)

title: The Sanguine Hibiscus
body: The sporelings of Sporeggar use the sanguine hibiscus for a number of purposes, and their supply is running low. The flowers used to grow as thick as shrubs, Gzhun'tt explains, but now that the marsh's water is falling they can be found only in the Underbog at Coilfang Reservoir, beneath Serpent Lake. Worse, the shamblers, bog giants and underbats down there are said to consider them a delicacy, so whoever would help must take the flowers from the creatures that eat them.

parts.body: The flowers would do nicely, Gzhun'tt said, but Sporeggar can always use more of them, and anyone who finds their way back into the Underbog is welcome to gather another bunch from its shamblers, bog giants and underbats and bring it home to the sporelings.
sources: quests 9715 and 9714 reward text (These will do nicely, but we can always use more. Perhaps you will find yourself in the Underbog again soon?)
quest 9714 completion text (We can still use more of the sanguine hibiscus from the shamblers, bog giants and underbats of the Underbog)
